title: Radical: Taking Back Your Faith from the American Dream
author: David Platt
target_audience: Churchgoers interested in deeper faith practice
Christians questioning materialism and cultural Christianity
Readers interested in missions and global Christianity
core_themes: Contrast between biblical Christianity and American consumer culture
The dangers of materialism and comfort
Global mission and caring for the poor
primary_purpose: To challenge Christians to examine how American culture has influenced their understanding and practice of faith, urging them to abandon comfortable, consumer-driven Christianity in favor of radical obedience to Jesus's teachings, particularly concerning sacrifice, generosity, and global mission.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, direct, urgent, and often confessional
structure_format.organization: Nine chapters plus introduction and conclusion, blending biblical exposition, personal stories, and challenges to readers
features: Personal anecdotes from the author’s ministry
Questions for reflection and practical application
A final 'Radical Experiment' to implement over a year

key_concepts_lessons: Following Jesus involves sacrificing comfort, wealth, and safety.
American cultural values sometimes undermine or obscure the Bible’s radical demands.
Faithful discipleship means putting Jesus above all else—including family, career, and the pursuit of the 'American Dream'.
Every Christian has a role in global mission and social justice.
Genuine faith is demonstrated in radical generosity, self-denial, and active commitment to the gospel.
notable_features: Includes real-world stories of radical Christian living
Closes with 'The Radical Experiment', a one-year challenge for readers
Addresses both personal and church-wide applications
Emphasizes biblical authority over cultural norms
cultural_historical_context: Written during the late 2000s, post-economic crash era, when questions about materialism and the nature of Christian faith in the affluent West were prominent. Platt, a young megachurch pastor, voices growing concerns about the alignment of American values with traditional Christian discipleship.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller within evangelical circles
Widely used in church small groups, book studies, and mission mobilization trainings
Sparked conversations and debates about materialism, cultural Christianity, and missions
Some critics argue the book's approach can be guilt-inducing or idealistic
comparable_titles: Crazy Love: Overwhelmed by a Relentless God by Francis Chan
Follow Me: A Call to Die. A Call to Live. by David Platt
Don’t Waste Your Life by John Piper
The Irresistible Revolution by Shane Claiborne
